You bring in investors who back companies directly, understand what each of them looks for, and introduce them to opportunities that fit. You also open new investor relationships every month, using the same approach that built your existing ones. You know which investors in your network have made a direct investment in the past year, what they invest in, and at what stage and check size. When a founder needs qualified investor meetings at short notice, you know whom to approach first. We are not raising a fund. Our investors invest directly in companies, so a network made up mainly of fund LPs or institutional mandates is not the right fit for this role, however strong it is. Our platform handles the pipeline, research and follow-up. Your time goes to investor conversations, and to judging which investors are ready to commit capital. You will work directly with the two co-founders and our investor team. The organisation is flat, so you will see first-hand how we screen opportunities, what we decline and why. Your current title matters less than the quality of your relationships. We are looking for someone who has built those relationships personally and can explain exactly how. WHAT YOU WILL OWN Your investor relationships. The investors you bring and those you add here, kept current and qualified. They remain yours. Network growth. New relationships every month with family offices, high-net-worth individuals and angel investors who are new to Pairs. Investor matching. A clear understanding of what each investor looks for, so the opportunities you share are relevant. Ongoing engagement. Staying useful to investors between opportunities, so they continue to work with us. YOU ARE A FIT IF YOU Have built your investor relationships personally, and can explain how each one began: direct outreach, referrals you cultivated, or events and networks you engaged with deliberately. Have taken at least one investor from a first conversation to a direct investment in a private round, and can walk us through the process. Understand what your investors invest in: stage, check size, sector, and the reasons they decline. Treat discretion as second nature. Please do not include any investor names in your application. Use AI tools daily, with clear judgement about where they improve your work and where they would compromise its quality. WHAT WE OFFER A fully remote, asynchronous role Direct access to the co-founders and our investor team Close collaboration with our internal team Live mandates from your first week, and access to the opportunities that clear our diligence Insight into our internal processes, including how we screen deal flow A base salary plus commission

9dac48975284b5f9.description: About Salehiya Healthcare Salehiya Healthcare, established in 1964, is a leading Saudi Arabian company specializing in the distribution of pharmaceuticals, medical and laboratory equipment, diagnostics, medical disposables, and hospital and consumer supplies. The company has evolved with the healthcare sector in Saudi Arabia, meeting the demands of a growing market. With over 1000 employees, Salehiya Healthcare operates from its main bases in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, alongside branches across the Kingdom to ensure comprehensive market coverage and efficient client services. The Role of Senior Compliance Specialist Salehiya Healthcare is seeking a Senior Compliance Specialist to join its team in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. This full-time role is central to supporting and enhancing the organization's compliance framework. The specialist will monitor adherence to applicable laws, regulations, policies, and ethical standards, identify compliance risks, and recommend effective controls and corrective actions. The objective is to safeguard the organization and foster a culture of integrity and accountability. Key Responsibilities Support the development and continuous improvement of the company’s Compliance and Ethics Program, including the Code of Conduct, policies, procedures, monitoring activities, training, and reporting channels. Participate in developing, implementing, and maintaining the company Code of Conduct, covering areas such as anti-corruption, fair competition, conflict of interest, and non-retaliation. Support the development, implementation, review, and update of compliance and ethics policies, including Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption, Business Expenses, and Conflict of Interest. Perform compliance risk assessments and contribute to the identification, evaluation, documentation, and monitoring of compliance risks and mitigating controls. Conduct compliance monitoring reviews and assessments to evaluate adherence to applicable laws, regulations, company policies, and ethical standards. Participate in the periodic review of company disbursements, business expenses, gifts, hospitality, sponsorships, and donations to ensure compliance with anti-bribery and anti-corruption requirements. Support the development and implementation of a formal process for reporting potential compliance incidents and conducting investigations. Support in conducting due diligence, screening, and compliance checks for new and existing third parties, vendors, business partners, and employees. Review and assess Conflict of Interest declarations, disclosures, incident reports, and third-party submissions. Support the development and implementation of a periodic compliance training and awareness plan for employees and relevant third parties. Prepare compliance reports, risk assessments, monitoring results, investigation summaries, and other documentation. Support the collection, analysis, and interpretation of compliance-related data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement. Maintain up-to-date knowledge of relevant laws, regulations, industry practices, healthcare compliance requirements, and anti-bribery and corruption standards. Qualifications and Experience A minimum of 3-5 years of experience in a compliance-related role. Demonstrated understanding of compliance frameworks, risk assessment methodologies, and regulatory requirements. Experience in developing and implementing compliance policies, procedures, and training programs. Strong analytical and investigative skills. Ability to prepare clear and concise reports and documentation. Work Environment and Culture Salehiya Healthcare is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace that values all employees. The company encourages creativity and innovation, particularly in technology, by utilizing current tools and staying ahead of industry trends. Comprehensive training programs and mentorship opportunities are provided to support professional growth and development, maintaining a welcoming atmosphere for everyone. The core values are driven by the purpose to elevate the healthcare experience in the Kingdom.

9d7640ef2c192b58.description: The Senior Specialist - Cloud Operation – Cloud Operations is responsible for supporting the day-to-day operation, reliability, governance, security, and optimization of Azure and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) environments. The role works closely with infrastructure, security, application, service desk, vendors, managed service providers, and business stakeholders to ensure cloud services are stable, secure, resilient, cost-effective, and aligned with business requirements. The role also supports Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) practices, including service availability, monitoring, incident response, reliability improvement, automation, and operational excellence. Key Responsibilities Support daily cloud operations across Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Monitor cloud infrastructure health, availability, performance, capacity, and incidents. Support SRE practices, including reliability monitoring, availability improvement, incident response, service health reviews, and operational automation. Manage incident response, service requests, escalations, and root cause analysis for cloud services. Support implementation and maintenance of cloud governance, policies, standards, tagging, and compliance controls. Review and optimize cloud cost, usage, reserved capacity, rightsizing, and resource cleanup. Coordinate with vendors, managed service providers, and internal teams to resolve operational issues. Support native backup, disaster recovery, high availability, and business continuity activities. Maintain cloud documentation, operational runbooks, architecture diagrams, and knowledge base articles. Support cloud security operations, including IAM reviews, network security, patching, vulnerability remediation, encryption, and access governance. Assist with automation and Infrastructure as Code adoption using tools such as Terraform. Track operational KPIs such as availability, incident resolution, SLA compliance, policy violations, cost optimization, reliability metrics, and documentation coverage. Participate in change management, release coordination, and operational readiness reviews. Support audits, compliance reviews, and risk remediation related to Azure and GCP cloud infrastructure. Required Skills and Experience Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in cloud operations, cloud engineering, infrastructure operations, SRE, or related technical roles. Hands-on knowledge of Microsoft Azure and/or Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Understanding of cloud networking, identity, compute, storage, monitoring, backup, security, and high availability. Experience with incident, problem, change, and service request management. Familiarity with SRE concepts, including availability, reliability, monitoring, alerting, incident response, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement. Familiarity with ITIL processes and IT service management tools. Good understanding of cloud security, IAM, RBAC, network security groups/firewalls, encryption, vulnerability management, and compliance controls. Ability to work with vendors, managed service providers, and cross-functional teams. Strong troubleshooting, communication, documentation, and stakeholder coordination skills. Experience with automation or scripting using tools such as Terraform, PowerShell, or Python is preferred.
